scenario: Amazon HM 追问：「这个配置冲突为什么拖到最终测试才发现？生命周期一开始就该考虑。」你确实是后期才发现的。
scenario_en: The Amazon hiring manager presses: "Why was this config conflict only caught at final testing? That is basic to consider at the start of the design phase." You really did find it late.
q: 被追问「为什么这么晚才发现」，第一句该说什么？
q_en: Pressed on why you caught it so late — what's your first sentence?
options: 承认当时自己对整个 flow 还不够熟、经验不足，所以没能在设计阶段提前观察到这个风险
prototype 阶段白名单只有 1% 商家，样本太小，跑出来是对的；实验放大后假设才失效
解释是 PM 的需求来得晚、上游没同步配置语义、排期又压得紧，所以没时间提前梳理组合
跳过原因直接讲 takeaway：以后设计评审就和 PM 摊开高风险组合，不解释当时为什么没发现
options_en: Admit you weren't familiar enough with the whole flow and lacked the experience to spot the risk at design time.
At prototype stage the whitelist was only 1% of sellers — too small a sample; the results looked right, and the assumption only broke once we scaled the experiment.
Blame the timeline: the PM's requirements landed late, upstream never shared the config semantics, and the schedule was tight, so nobody mapped the combinations.
Skip the cause and jump to the takeaway: from now on design review covers high-risk combinations with the PM — without explaining why it was missed.
tradeoff: 认知演进 vs 承认不熟：说不熟听着诚实，代价是它被记成对我经验的评价，而不是一次可解释的判断。
why: 把「我不熟」换成「样本规模决定的认知演进」：早期 1% 白名单看不出冲突，规模一上来假设才失效。
why_en: Instead of admitting I wasn't familiar with the flow, I reframe it as evidence that changed — at one percent of sellers the data looked fine, and the assumption only broke once we scaled up.
whenOtherWins: 如果追问的模块你确实没参与、在职责边界之外，就直说不了解，并立刻给出你会怎么查。
optionMeanings: 把原因归到自己的熟悉度和经验上
用早期样本量解释判断当时为什么成立
把原因推给 PM、上游团队和排期
只讲改进措施，跳过原因
optionMeanings_en: Pin the cause on your own familiarity and experience.
Explain why the judgement held given the early sample size.
Push the cause onto the PM, upstream team, and schedule.
Give only the improvement and skip the cause.
optionDirectness: 只有在内部复盘、对方要的是自我批评时才合适
抓住了「结论随证据规模变化」这条可验证的线
错在归因方向：全推给别人，显不出自己的判断
错在时机：原因没交代，takeaway 就没有落点
optionDirectness_en: Only fits an internal retro where self-criticism is what's wanted.
Catches the verifiable line: the conclusion changed when the sample grew.
Wrong on attribution — pushing it all outward shows no judgement of your own.
Wrong on timing — a takeaway with no cause behind it has nothing to land on.
optionScenarioImpacts: 面试官记下「职场经验少」，这轮最大的扣分点
问题从能力评价变成一次实验设计的讨论
听起来在甩锅，追问只会更密
对方会再追一次「所以当初为什么没发现」
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The interviewer writes down "limited work experience" — the biggest deduction of the round.
The question shifts from judging your ability to discussing experiment design.
It reads as blame-shifting and invites even harder follow-ups.
They just ask again: so why wasn't it caught at the time?

q: Amazon 教练点名的两句面试禁语是什么？卡住时能用它们垫场吗？
q_en: Which two phrases did the coach ban outright, and can you use them to fill a stall?
text: 两句绝对不能出口：{{我不知道 / 我对这个不太熟}}，和{{谁谁让我做，所以我就干了}}；被问卡住、僵在那里时也{{不能}}用它们填空。
text_en: Two phrases to never say: {{I don't know / I'm not that familiar with this}}, and {{someone told me to do it, so I did}}; even when you freeze mid-question you still {{cannot}} use them as filler.
why: 第一句让人判断我没在职场被毒打过，第二句等于承认没有自己的判断。宁可沉默两秒，也不要用它们垫场。
why_en: The first phrase reads as someone with little real work experience and the second says I have no judgement of my own, so two seconds of silence beats either of them.

scenario: 面试官问：「这个技术方案当时是谁定的？你为什么选它？」实际上是 tech lead 拍的板，你照着实现。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks: "Who decided on this technical approach, and why did you pick it?" In reality the tech lead made the call and you implemented it.
q: 「方案是谁定的」这类追问怎么答？
q_en: How do you answer "who decided on this approach"?
options: 如实说是 tech lead 定的方向，我按他的要求实现，为什么选它我当时没参与讨论
说成是我自己独立拍板的，把 tech lead 的判断算到自己头上，显得更有主导权
说清取舍：为什么这条路在当时的排期下更快落地，以及我补了哪一层兜底
绕开方案归属，直接讲上线结果和指标，不谈当时为什么选这条路、谁定的
options_en: Say plainly that the tech lead set the direction, you implemented it, and you weren't part of the why-this-approach discussion.
Claim you made the call yourself, taking credit for the tech lead's judgement so you look more in charge.
Give the tradeoff: why that path shipped faster under the schedule, and which safety net you added on top.
Dodge the ownership question and go straight to launch results and metrics, never saying why that path or who chose it.
tradeoff: 说出自己的理解 vs 复述分工：如实交代谁拍板听着老实，代价是被记成「没有独立判断」。
why: 「别人让我做的」等于交出判断力。方案不是我拍的板，我也要说得出它的取舍，以及我在里面加了什么。
why_en: Saying someone told me to do it hands away my judgement, so even when I didn't make the call I still explain the tradeoff and what I added on top.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官在问的是决策流程和汇报关系，就说清谁拍板——但仍要补一句你自己的判断。
optionMeanings: 只交代分工，不给自己的判断
把别人的决定说成自己的
复述这条路的取舍和自己的补强
跳过方案来源，只讲结果
optionMeanings_en: Report the division of labour and offer no judgement.
Present someone else's decision as your own.
Lay out the tradeoff of that path and what you strengthened.
Skip where the design came from and give results only.
optionDirectness: 错在层次：交代了事实，没交代思考
只有你真的拍过板时才成立，否则一追就穿
把「不是我定的」和「我有判断」两件事分开说清了
错在时机：结果好不代表你参与过决策
optionDirectness_en: Wrong level — you report the facts but not the thinking.
Only holds if you truly made the call; otherwise one follow-up exposes it.
Separates "I didn't decide it" from "I still had a view" cleanly.
Wrong timing — a good outcome doesn't show you were in the decision.
optionScenarioImpacts: 被记成执行者，Ownership 类问题拿不到分
追问细节时对不上，可信度整段崩
既没抢功，也证明了自己在思考
面试官会直接再问一次「你的判断是什么」
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You're logged as an executor and score nothing on ownership-style questions.
The details won't line up on follow-up and the whole answer loses credibility.
You neither steal credit nor look passive — you show you were thinking.
The interviewer simply asks again: so what was your view?

scenario: Amazon 要求面试官把问答记成接近逐字的记录而不是摘要；debrief 上所有面试官互读记录，由 bar raiser 主持并对录用有否决权。
scenario_en: Amazon asks interviewers to write near-verbatim transcripts rather than summaries; at the debrief every interviewer reads the others' notes, and the bar raiser runs the room with veto power.
q: 在这套记录机制下，一句「我对这个不太熟」会怎样传播？
q_en: Under that note-taking system, how far does one "I'm not that familiar with it" travel?
options: 只留在这一轮的评分里，其他面试官看不到，后面几轮表现好就能盖过去
recruiter 会先过滤掉负面措辞，只把技术结论和评级汇总给 bar raiser 做参考，不带原话
要在同一轮里重复三次以上，才会被写进最终的书面反馈
被原样记进这一轮的逐字记录，debrief 上全组读到，变成一个负面 data point
options_en: It stays inside that round's score, other interviewers never see it, and strong later rounds cover it.
The recruiter filters out negative wording first and passes only the technical conclusions and ratings to the bar raiser, without the original quotes.
It only reaches the written feedback if you repeat it three or more times in the same round.
It goes into that round's near-verbatim notes, the whole loop reads it at the debrief, and it becomes a negative data point.
why: 面试官的笔记接近逐字稿、debrief 上互相传阅，所以一句自我否定会被原样读出来。这就是禁语要练成条件反射的原因。
why_en: Amazon interviewers write near-verbatim notes that everyone reads at the debrief, so one self-deprecating sentence gets quoted back and turns into a negative data point.

termDefinitions.meaning: 外组的资深面试官，主持 debrief、负责横向定级把关，对录用有否决权。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bar raiser is a senior interviewer from another team who runs the debrief and can veto the hire.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试结束后所有面试官碰头、互读各自记录并给出录用结论的会议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A debrief is the meeting after the loop where all interviewers read each other's notes and decide together.

termDefinitions.meaning: Amazon 的领导力准则；每位面试官按分到的几条准则收集证据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LP stands for Leadership Principles, the rubric each Amazon interviewer collects evidence against.

optionMeanings: 认为负面信息只留在本轮
认为 recruiter 会做一层过滤
认为要重复多次才被记录
认为逐字记录会被全组读到
optionMeanings_en: Assumes negative signal stays inside one round.
Assumes the recruiter filters the wording first.
Assumes it must repeat several times to be recorded.
Assumes near-verbatim notes get read by the whole loop.
optionDirectness: 误判了传播范围：debrief 就是为了打通各轮
误判了角色：recruiter 不改面试官的记录
误判了阈值：一句就够，笔记不做频次统计
对上了逐字记录 + 全员互读这两条机制
optionDirectness_en: Misjudges the blast radius — the debrief exists precisely to join the rounds up.
Misjudges the role — recruiters don't edit interviewer notes.
Misjudges the threshold — one line is enough; notes don't count repetitions.
Matches both mechanisms: verbatim notes plus everyone reading everyone.
optionScenarioImpacts: 会让你以为后面几轮能补回来，从而不改口
会让你依赖一个并不存在的缓冲层
会让你觉得说一次没关系，风险被低估
解释了为什么这句要练成条件反射
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Makes you think later rounds can fix it, so you never change the phrasing.
Makes you rely on a buffer layer that doesn't exist.
Makes one slip feel harmless and understates the risk.
Explains why the banned phrase has to become a reflex.

scenario: Amazon Round 1 你在讲 Meta onboarding 故事，面试官追问「往 context 里加字段后 token 大概多大？对推理有什么影响？」你没量过这个数。
scenario_en: In Amazon Round 1 you're telling the Meta onboarding story and the interviewer asks: "How big was the token count once you added fields to the context, and how did that hit inference?" You never measured it.
q: 被追问一个自己没量过的数字，怎么接？
q_en: How do you handle a follow-up asking for a number you never measured?
options: 现推量级：一句话 50–100 词 × 2–3 token ≈ 200–300，加模板约 1000–2000，可忽略
直说我从没查过 token size，这个数得回去翻监控面板和离线日志才能给出准确答案
报一个很大的数字，比如十几万 token，让这段故事听起来更有规模感、更有说服力
绕开数字不答，把话题转到字段质量上，只讲我们后来砍掉了低质量字段、让 context 更干净更聚焦，指望他不再追量级
options_en: Derive the order of magnitude live: 50–100 words at 2–3 tokens each is roughly 200–300, about 1000–2000 with the prompt template, which is negligible for inference.
Say plainly you never checked the token size and would need the dashboards and offline logs to give an accurate number.
Throw out a big number like a couple hundred thousand tokens so the story sounds larger and more impressive.
Avoid the number entirely and pivot to field quality, saying only that you later cut low-quality fields to keep the context cleaner and tighter, hoping he drops the sizing question.
tradeoff: 现推量级 vs 承认没查过：承认更安全，代价是这个故事被判定为「没真正做透」。
why: 被追问数字时空白比估算不准更糟。用「输入长度 × 每词 token 数 + 模板开销」现推一个量级，再说它对延迟和成本意味着什么。
why_en: Going blank on a number costs more than an imperfect estimate, so I derive it live from input length times tokens per word plus template overhead, then say what it means for latency and cost.
whenOtherWins: 如果这个数会直接决定对方的方案选择（容量、报价），就说明这是估算，并给出你会怎么实测。
optionMeanings: 用一条可复述的公式现推量级
承认没测过，把答案推到会后
凭感觉给一个夸大的数字
换个维度回答，避开数字本身
optionMeanings_en: Derive the magnitude live from a formula you can repeat.
Admit you never measured it and defer the answer.
Guess a inflated number to sound impressive.
Answer on a different axis and skip the number.
optionDirectness: 把「没量过」变成「能算出来」，判断力还在
只有当精确值会影响对方决策时才该这么答
错在可验证性：一追口径就穿
错在方向：他问的是量级，不是取舍
optionDirectness_en: Turns "never measured" into "can be derived" and keeps your judgement visible.
Only right when the exact value would change their decision.
Fails on verifiability — one question about the method exposes it.
Wrong axis — he asked for magnitude, not for your tradeoff.
optionScenarioImpacts: 追问从考数字变成看你怎么估
面试官记下「自己的项目也说不出量级」
下一个追问就会问你怎么算的，直接崩
对方会再问一次数字，你还是得答
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The follow-up shifts from testing a number to watching how you estimate.
The interviewer notes you can't size your own project.
The next follow-up asks how you got it and the answer collapses.
They simply ask for the number again and you still have to answer.

scenario: Assembled 那轮你讲 Meta toggle 故事，被问「activation 到底提升了几个点？」你回了「I don't remember, maybe a few percent」。
scenario_en: On the Assembled call you told the Meta toggle story and were asked how many points activation improved. You said "I don't remember, maybe a few percent."
q: 故事里的关键指标一时记不清时该怎么说？
q_en: What do you say when you can't recall the key metric in your own story?
options: 回一句「记不太清，大概就几个百分点吧」，把不确定如实交代出去，等对方追问时再回去补
说这属于公司内部指标、不方便对外透露，只讲做法和上线机制，跳过所有结果数字
换成定性影响：更多商家真正用上了 AI agent，具体百分比就先不提了，讲讲机制
给区间和口径：约 50% 提到 53–55%，漏斗上 toggle 是主要掉点
options_en: Say "I don't remember exactly, maybe a few percent" and hand the uncertainty over, filling in details if they push.
Say it's an internal metric you can't share externally, and cover only the approach and rollout mechanics instead.
Switch to qualitative impact — more businesses actually turned the AI agent on — and leave the percentage out while you explain the mechanism.
Give a range and how it was measured: roughly 50% up to 53–55%, with the toggle step as the main drop-off in the funnel.
tradeoff: 有信心的区间 vs 老实说记不清：说记不清最安全，代价是整个故事从「有证据」降级成「一个说法」。
why: 没有数字的故事是没有证据的主张。给一个有信心的区间并说清口径，比「maybe a few percent」强十倍。
why_en: A story without a number is a claim without evidence, so give a confident range and say how it was measured instead of hedging with "maybe a few percent."
whenOtherWins: 如果这个数确实受保密约束，就说明保密边界，再给一个可公开的相对量级（如「低个位数百分点」）。
optionMeanings: 把不确定原样交出去
用保密理由跳过结果
把结果换成定性描述
给区间并说明它怎么量的
optionMeanings_en: Hand the uncertainty over as-is.
Use confidentiality to skip the outcome.
Replace the number with a qualitative claim.
Give a range and say how it was measured.
optionDirectness: 错在证据层：故事的结论没有落点
只有真的受合规约束时才成立
错在粒度：定性描述换不来可比性
把主张和量化口径绑在一起，可被追问
optionDirectness_en: Fails on evidence — the story's conclusion has nothing under it.
Only holds when a real confidentiality rule applies.
Wrong grain — a qualitative claim gives nothing to compare against.
Ties the claim to a measurement you can be questioned on.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方记下「讲的是别人的项目」
听起来像在回避，追问反而更细
面试官还是会追一次具体数
故事从说法变成有证据的结论
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They note it down as "telling someone else's project."
It reads as dodging and invites sharper follow-ups.
The interviewer just asks for the number again.
The story turns from a claim into an evidenced result.

scenario: 面试官追问「为什么当时没看出来」，你脑子里第一反应是「我那会儿还不熟」——这句是禁语，要用一个可解释的框架顶上。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks why you didn't see it at the time and your reflex is "I wasn't familiar with it yet" — a banned phrase you must replace with an explainable frame.
q: 把「卡住时的替代框架」四步排成正确顺序。
q_en: Put the four steps of the stall-recovery frame in the right order.
steps: 说清后来什么推翻了它：实验放大、商家变多之后假设不成立
先接住问题，说出当时所处的阶段和条件：prototype，白名单只有 1% 商家
收一句现在的做法：设计评审阶段就和 PM 摊开高风险组合
说当时依据什么判断：那批数据跑出来结果是对的
why: 顺序是阶段 → 当时的依据 → 什么推翻了它 → 现在怎么做。全程说的是证据的变化，不是我的能力。
why_en: The order is stage, the evidence I had then, what overturned it, and what I do now — every step talks about evidence changing, not about my ability.

scenario: 面试官追问一个细节，你脑子里没有现成答案，只有几秒钟决定走哪条路——而「我不知道」是禁语。
scenario_en: A follow-up lands on a detail you have no ready answer for, and you have seconds to choose a path — while "I don't know" is off the table.
q: 追问落在你答不上来的细节上，怎么分流？
q_en: When a follow-up hits a detail you can't answer, how do you triage?
options: 先分它是否在我负责的范围：在内走「阶段→依据→推翻→现在」，在外说清边界并给排查路径
一律现场编一个听起来合理的答案，赌对方不会再往下追第二层细节，也不会回头核对口径和数字
一律直说不知道，保持诚实，把要不要换一道题的判断权完整交回给面试官去决定
把话题拉回自己准备好的结果和指标，不正面回答这个细节，等他自己放弃这条追问线
options_en: First sort by scope: inside your area, run stage → evidence → what overturned it → what you do now; outside it, name the boundary and give your investigation path.
Always improvise something plausible and bet they won't push to a second layer of detail.
Always say you don't know, stay honest, and hand back the decision of whether to swap the question.
Steer back to the results and metrics you rehearsed, never facing the detail, and wait for them to drop it.
tradeoff: 先分范围再选路 vs 一律用同一句应付：统一话术省脑力，代价是范围内的题被当成不懂，范围外的题被当成瞎编。
why: 先判断这个细节在不在我负责的范围：在内用证据框架顶上，在外说边界并给排查路径。两条路都不需要说「我不知道」。
why_en: I first check whether the detail sits inside my scope: inside it I answer with the evidence frame, outside it I name the boundary and how I'd investigate, so neither path needs "I don't know."
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官已经明说「不知道也没关系，我想看你怎么想」，那就直接把推理过程说出声，不必套框架。
optionMeanings: 按职责范围分两条应对路线
编一个听起来合理的答案
统一用诚实的「不知道」应对
转移话题回到准备好的内容
optionMeanings_en: Split into two responses based on scope.
Invent something that sounds plausible.
Fall back on an honest "I don't know" every time.
Redirect to material you already rehearsed.
optionDirectness: 区分了两种失败：越界瞎编 vs 界内空白
错在可验证性：第二层追问立刻拆穿
错在措辞：这正是教练点名的禁语
错在时机：躲掉一次，追问还会回来
optionDirectness_en: Separates two different failures: bluffing outside scope versus blanking inside it.
Fails on verifiability — a second-layer follow-up exposes it immediately.
Fails on wording — this is exactly the phrase the coach banned.
Fails on timing — you dodge once and the follow-up comes back.
optionScenarioImpacts: 两种情况下都还有话可说，节奏不断
编错了比承认更糟，可信度整段掉
被记成经验不足，这轮最大扣分点
对方会认定你在回避核心细节
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You still have something to say either way and the rhythm holds.
A wrong guess is worse than admitting it and takes the whole answer's credibility.
You get logged as inexperienced — the round's biggest deduction.
They conclude you're avoiding the core detail.

scenario: TaskRabbit 那轮进行到 42 分钟，招聘人暂停通话说「你每道题前都停很久」，并直接问你是不是在用 AI，还说后面几轮会上检测。
scenario_en: Forty-two minutes into the TaskRabbit call the recruiter paused to say "you pause a lot before every answer," asked outright if you were using AI, and said detection would be added in later rounds.
q: 被当面问「你是不是在用 AI」，当下怎么回应？
q_en: Asked point-blank whether you're using AI — what do you do in that moment?
options: 笑一下带过去，说没有，然后赶紧回到上一个技术问题继续往下答，当这段插曲没发生过
直接接住并给可验证的解释：我在脑子里先译成英文，节奏确实慢；接下来我先给结论再展开
反问她为什么会这么判断，请她说明具体是哪几道题让她产生了这个印象，然后再决定怎么解释
承认自己准备了笔记，说只是在照着提纲看，问她介不介意自己边看边答，把选择权交给她
options_en: Laugh it off, say no, and hurry back to the previous technical question.
Take it head-on with a checkable explanation: you translate into English in your head, which is genuinely slow, and from here you'll lead with the conclusion then expand.
Turn it around and ask why she thinks that, asking which questions gave her the impression.
Admit you prepared notes, say you're just reading an outline, and ask whether she minds you consulting them.
tradeoff: 当场解释并改节奏 vs 否认带过：否认最省事，代价是怀疑没被消除，之后每次停顿都在给她的假设加分。
why: 被点名时要给一个可验证的解释，并立刻改变节奏——先给结论再展开，让停顿模式当场消失，而不是否认了事。
why_en: When they name it, give a checkable reason and change the rhythm on the spot — lead with the conclusion, then expand — so the pause pattern disappears instead of just being denied.
whenOtherWins: 如果你确实用了辅助工具，唯一体面的路是承认并说明用途；在有检测的后续轮次里硬否认只会更糟。
optionMeanings: 否认并转回上一个话题
给出原因并当场改变节奏
把举证责任推回给对方
承认在照稿并请求许可
optionMeanings_en: Deny it and go back to the previous topic.
Give the reason and change your rhythm right there.
Push the burden of proof back onto her.
Admit you're reading and ask permission.
optionDirectness: 错在证据：光否认改变不了她看到的模式
同时处理了怀疑的来源和行为本身
只有当你确信是误会且有余地时才合适
错在方向：照稿正是她怀疑的那件事
optionDirectness_en: Fails on evidence — denial doesn't change the pattern she observed.
Handles both the source of the suspicion and the behaviour itself.
Only fits when you're sure it's a misread and there's room to push back.
Wrong direction — reading from a script is the very thing she suspects.
optionScenarioImpacts: 怀疑留着，后面每次停顿都在坐实
她能立刻看到节奏变化，怀疑被行为反驳
对方会觉得你在辩护而不是在解决
等于承认了她的判断，后续轮次更难过
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The suspicion stays and every later pause confirms it.
She sees the rhythm change immediately and the behaviour disproves the doubt.
You come across as defending yourself rather than fixing it.
You essentially confirm her read and make later rounds harder.

q: 为什么「每题前长停顿」会被读成在用 AI？
q_en: Why does a long pause before every answer read as AI assistance?
text: 实时辅助工具要 {{3–5}} 秒完成转写和生成，于是延迟{{不随题目难度变化}}——难题易题一样慢；候选人常靠{{复述问题}}填这段空档，而这正是对方盯的信号。
text_en: Live assistance tools need {{3–5}} seconds to transcribe and generate, so the latency {{doesn't track question difficulty}} — easy and hard questions stall the same; candidates often {{repeat the question back}} to cover the gap, and that is exactly the tell interviewers watch for.
why: 他们看的不是停顿有多长，是停顿的模式。让延迟随题目难度自然变化——简单题秒答、难题才停——模式对了怀疑就散了。
why_en: They aren't watching how long you pause but whether the pause tracks difficulty, so answer easy questions instantly and save the thinking time for hard ones.

scenario: 你习惯把答案整句写在笔记里、面试时照着念，上一轮因此被怀疑在读 AI 生成的稿子。
scenario_en: You write full sentences in your notes and read from them during calls, which is why the last round suspected you of reading AI output.
q: 面试笔记该做成什么形态？
q_en: What form should interview notes take?
options: 整句写好逐字稿，紧张时能直接照着念，保证一个要点都不漏掉，语序和数字也不会临场乱掉次序和口径
把常见问题的答案打印出来贴在屏幕两侧，随时扫一眼就能找到对应的那一条来照着说
开一个文档实时记面试官的问题，边记边组织语言，答完之后再补充细节
只留关键词，比如 trade-offs: speed vs safety，靠它触发练过的说法
options_en: Write full scripted sentences so you can read them when nervous and never miss a point.
Print answers to common questions and tape them beside the screen, glancing over to find the right one.
Keep a doc open and type the interviewer's questions live, organizing your answer as you type and filling in after.
Keep only keywords, like "trade-offs: speed vs safety," to trigger phrasing you've already rehearsed.
tradeoff: 关键词触发 vs 逐字稿：逐字稿保证不漏点，代价是语流变成朗读，正是被怀疑用 AI 的那个特征。
why: 整句笔记一定会变成朗读，眼神和节奏都藏不住。关键词只负责触发，句子必须是当场生成的。
why_en: Full-sentence notes always turn into reading aloud and your eyes and rhythm give it away, so keywords should only trigger phrasing you generate live.
whenOtherWins: 只有需要精确说出的东西——公司名、指标口径、薪资区间——才值得写成完整句子。
optionMeanings: 把答案写成可朗读的完整稿
把答案库贴在视线周边随时查
边听边打字整理对方的问题
只写触发词，句子现场生成
optionMeanings_en: Write the answer as a readable script.
Post an answer bank around your screen to scan.
Type out the interviewer's question while listening.
Write only trigger words and generate sentences live.
optionDirectness: 错在形态：能念的东西一定会被念出来
错在动作：找条目的眼动最容易被看到
错在注意力：打字会吃掉听和答的带宽
留下触发点又逼你即时组织语言
optionDirectness_en: Wrong form — anything readable will get read.
Wrong motion — the eye movement while hunting for an entry is the most visible tell.
Wrong attention budget — typing eats the bandwidth for listening and answering.
Keeps the trigger but forces you to compose on the spot.
optionScenarioImpacts: 语调变平、停顿变长，怀疑加深
眼睛离屏、来回扫，正是检测点
回答慢半拍，还容易漏掉追问
语流自然，停顿随难度变化
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Your intonation flattens and pauses lengthen, deepening the suspicion.
Your eyes leave the camera and scan sideways — exactly what they look for.
You answer half a beat late and start missing follow-ups.
Speech sounds natural and pauses vary with difficulty.

scenario: 面试官抛来一个你没准备过的设计问题，你确实需要五到十秒才能组织出第一句——但上一轮已经因为「每题前长停顿」被怀疑用 AI。
scenario_en: The interviewer throws a design question you haven't prepared and you genuinely need five to ten seconds to form the first sentence — but the last round already suspected AI because you paused before every answer.
q: 需要超过两秒的思考时间时，怎么合法地争取？
q_en: When you genuinely need more than two seconds, how do you buy that time legitimately?
options: 把这五到十秒安静地撑完，沉默本身不算填充词，等自己完全想清楚了再开口回答
先说一句「让我想一下」，然后安静地把整个答案在脑子里过完，再一次性讲出来
把正在做的判断说出声：我先当成读多写少来看，先定读路径，再回来看一致性
请对方把问题再说一遍，用他重复的这段时间在脑子里组织好自己的答案
options_en: Sit through the five to ten seconds in silence — silence isn't verbal filler — and speak only once you've fully worked it out.
Say "let me think about that," then run the whole answer in your head silently and deliver it in one go.
Narrate the judgement you're making: I'll treat this as read-heavy first, settle the read path, then come back to consistency.
Ask them to repeat the question and use the time they spend repeating it to organize your answer.
tradeoff: 出声推理 vs 静默思考：静默能想得更完整，代价是那段空白正好长得像在等工具出答案。
why: 超过两秒的沉默会被读成在等外部答案。把正在做的判断说出声——先框定问题类型、再定第一步——时间买到了，说的还都是有效信息。
why_en: Silence past two seconds reads as waiting for an answer from somewhere else, so narrate the judgement instead — frame the problem type, then name your first step — and the time you buy is still useful information.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需要一两秒，就直接沉默——短停顿读作在思考，比出声铺垫更干净。
optionMeanings: 用长沉默换完整的腹稿
先给一句预告，再静默思考
边推理边说，把过程交出去
让对方重复来换取时间
optionMeanings_en: Trade a long silence for a complete draft.
Announce that you're thinking, then think silently.
Reason out loud and hand over the process.
Buy time by having them repeat the question.
optionDirectness: 错在长度：这正是被怀疑的那个空白模式
错在效果：预告只是给沉默换了个包装
空白被有信息量的推理填满，还能被打断纠偏
错在次数：反复要求重复会被读成没在听
optionDirectness_en: Wrong length — this is exactly the blank pattern that drew suspicion.
Ineffective — announcing it just repackages the same silence.
Fills the gap with real reasoning they can interrupt and redirect.
Wrong frequency — repeated requests to repeat read as not listening.
optionScenarioImpacts: 怀疑被再加固一次，之后每题都被盯着
对方仍然只听到一段空白，判断不变
对方看得到你在想什么，还能中途给方向
对方开始怀疑你的听力或专注度
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The suspicion hardens and every later answer gets watched.
They still hear only a blank, so their read doesn't change.
They can see what you're weighing and can steer you mid-answer.
They start doubting your listening or your focus.

scenario: Gamma 那轮面试官问「你做过最复杂的系统是什么」，你开口第一句是「That's a challenging question」。
scenario_en: At Gamma the interviewer asked what the most complex system you'd built was, and your first words were "That's a challenging question."
q: 这类问题的第一句该是什么？
q_en: What should the first sentence of that answer be?
options: 先用一句 That's a great question 接住，给自己两三秒时间组织语言和思路
先说一句「这个我得想一下」，然后沉默十几秒把整个答案在脑子里过完再开口
直接给主张：我做过最复杂的是 GMV Max 的状态机，三个策略共享同一套 API
把问题原样复述一遍确认自己理解对了，然后再开始组织并给出正式回答
options_en: Buy time with "That's a great question" to get two or three seconds to organize your thoughts.
Say "let me think about that," then go silent for a dozen seconds while you run the whole answer in your head.
Lead with the claim: the most complex thing I built was the GMV Max state machine, where three strategies shared one API.
Repeat the question back to confirm you understood it, and only then start organizing and giving the real answer.
tradeoff: 直接给主张 vs 先垫一句：垫场买来两三秒，代价是开场就被读成准备不足。
why: 第一句必须是一个主张，不是对问题的评价。允许的是两秒沉默，不允许的是用语言填空。
why_en: The first sentence has to be a claim, not a comment on the question — two seconds of silence is fine, filling the gap with words is not.
whenOtherWins: 只有当问题真有歧义时，才用一句具体澄清代替主张：「你问的是读路径还是写路径？」
optionMeanings: 用评价句垫场换思考时间
用长沉默换完整的腹稿
第一句就给出具体结论
复述问题确认理解
optionMeanings_en: Use a compliment as filler to buy thinking time.
Trade a long silence for a fully drafted answer.
Put a concrete conclusion in the first sentence.
Repeat the question to confirm understanding.
optionDirectness: 错在信息量：这句话对面试官零价值
错在长度：超过两秒就成了尴尬空档
把系统名和难点压进一句，对方能直接记
错在动作：复述现在还是拖时间的信号
optionDirectness_en: Fails on information — the sentence gives the interviewer nothing.
Fails on length — past two seconds it becomes an awkward gap.
Packs the system name and the hard part into one line they can write down.
Wrong move — repeating the question now also reads as stalling.
optionScenarioImpacts: 被记成没准备好，还浪费了开场
长空档会被当成在等外部答案
面试官立刻知道该往哪儿追问
同时踩中没准备和疑似用 AI 两个判断
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You get logged as unprepared and waste the opening.
A long gap reads as waiting for an answer from somewhere else.
The interviewer immediately knows where to dig.
You trigger both the unprepared read and the AI suspicion at once.

scenario: Gamma 面试官问数据建模，你开口是「Relational data model and relational data...」，把问题原样念了一遍。
scenario_en: The Gamma interviewer asked about data modeling and you opened with "Relational data model and relational data..." — echoing the question back word for word.
q: 复述问题这个习惯，现在为什么特别危险？
q_en: Why is echoing the question back especially risky now?
options: 它是 AI 辅助候选人拖时间的典型动作，检测方把它当成信号
它会让面试官觉得你在质疑他的表述，显得不够礼貌也不够自信
它会占用回答时间，一场面试因此少答一两道有价值的问题
它会把问题的措辞固定住，让你的回答答不出更宽一些的适用范围
options_en: It's the classic stalling move of AI-assisted candidates, and interviewers treat it as a tell.
It makes the interviewer feel you're questioning their wording, which reads as impolite and unconfident.
It eats answering time, costing you one or two valuable questions over the interview.
It locks in their phrasing and keeps your answer from covering a broader range.
tradeoff: 直接给主张 vs 复述问题：复述能确认理解，代价是同时踩中「准备不足」和「疑似用 AI」两个判断。
why: 复述以前只是准备不足的信号，现在还是「等工具出答案」的典型动作。要么直接给主张，要么只澄清你不确定的那半句。
why_en: Echoing the question used to only signal poor preparation, but now it also reads as waiting for a tool, so lead with a claim or clarify just the part you're unsure of.
whenOtherWins: 如果问题真有歧义，就复述你不确定的那半句并请对方确认，而不是整句照念。
optionMeanings: 把它归到拖时间信号这一类
把它归到礼貌与自信问题
把它归到时间成本问题
把它归到答案范围被限制
optionMeanings_en: Classifies it as a stalling signal.
Classifies it as a politeness and confidence issue.
Classifies it as a time-cost issue.
Classifies it as narrowing your answer's scope.
optionDirectness: 对上了现在最贵的那个误判：疑似作弊
误判了性质：对方并不觉得被质疑
代价真实但很小，不是主要风险
方向反了：复述不会限制你的答案
optionDirectness_en: Matches the costliest misread today: suspected cheating.
Misreads the effect — they don't feel challenged by it.
A real but minor cost, not the main risk.
Backwards — repeating the question doesn't narrow your answer.
optionScenarioImpacts: 解释了为什么这个老习惯代价变高了
会让你只改语气，不改这个动作
会让你以为压缩时间就够了
会让你去改答案结构，改错了地方
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Explains why an old habit suddenly costs more.
Leads you to soften your tone but keep the habit.
Leads you to think trimming time is enough.
Sends you to restructure the answer — the wrong fix.

q: 面试里允许的停顿和不允许的填充分别是什么？
q_en: What kind of pause is allowed in an interview, and what kind of filler is not?
text: 允许的是 {{2 秒沉默}}；不允许的是用语言填空——{{That's a challenging question}} 这类评价句，和把问题{{原样复述}}一遍。
text_en: Allowed: {{two seconds of silence}}. Not allowed: filling the gap with words — comment-on-the-question openers like {{"That's a challenging question"}}, or {{repeating the question}} back verbatim.
why: 沉默两秒读作在思考，语言填充读作在拖时间。练到每类问题的第一句都是直接主张，填充就没有位置了。
why_en: Two seconds of silence reads as thinking while verbal filler reads as stalling, so drill each question type until the first sentence is always a direct claim.

scenario: Amazon 6 月那轮，你把 Kahn 拓扑排序说成了 DFS，面试官提示「Are you sure?」，你把整段逻辑从头重讲了三遍。
scenario_en: In the June Amazon round you called Kahn's topological sort "DFS," the interviewer hinted "Are you sure?", and you re-explained the whole logic three times from the top.
q: 说错一个术语之后，正确的纠正方式是什么？
q_en: After misnaming a term, what's the right way to correct yourself?
options: 说一句 sorry, maybe I start this question again，然后从头把整段思路重新讲一遍
先不动，等把代码写完再回头统一纠正，避免中途打断自己的节奏和思路
用一个从句改口：用队列逐层处理，所以这是 BFS，然后继续往下讲
承认自己这两个概念一直分不清，说完之后再问面试官要不要换一道题
options_en: Say "sorry, maybe I start this question again" and re-explain the whole approach from the beginning.
Leave it, finish writing the code, then correct everything at once so you don't break your own rhythm.
Fix it in one clause — "it processes level by level with a queue, so this is BFS" — and keep going.
Admit you've always mixed the two concepts up, then ask the interviewer if they'd rather switch questions.
tradeoff: 从句改口 vs 从头重讲：重讲让叙述更完整，代价是同一段逻辑讲三遍，时间和信心一起丢。
why: 一个干净的从句纠正，然后往下走。重启整段会把一次口误放大成「不自信 + 概念不清」两个信号。
why_en: Correct it in one clean clause and move on, because restarting the whole explanation turns a single slip into two signals: low confidence and shaky concepts.
whenOtherWins: 只有当错的是前提——算法选错、需求理解反了——才值得停下来重新开一段。
optionMeanings: 推倒重来，重新组织整段
推迟纠正，先把代码写完
就地改口，一句话带过
把口误升级成能力自陈
optionMeanings_en: Scrap it and reorganize the whole explanation.
Defer the correction until the code is done.
Fix it in place with a single clause.
Escalate a slip into a statement about your ability.
optionDirectness: 错在粒度：一个词的错，赔上整段时间
错在时机：面试官已经提示了，拖着更糟
只改那个词，其余叙述完整保留
错在措辞：这一句直接落进禁语区
optionDirectness_en: Wrong grain — one wrong word costs you the whole explanation's time.
Wrong timing — they already hinted, so delaying makes it worse.
Fixes only the word and leaves the rest of the narrative intact.
Wrong wording — that sentence lands straight in banned-phrase territory.
optionScenarioImpacts: 同一段逻辑讲三遍，编码时间被吃掉
面试官会以为你没听懂他的提示
口误被封在一个从句里，节奏不断
把一次口误变成一条能力上的负面记录
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You explain the same logic three times and lose the coding budget.
The interviewer thinks you missed their hint.
The slip stays boxed in one clause and the rhythm holds.
A single slip becomes a written note about your ability.

scenario: Round 3 结尾，白板权限故障已由 HM 解决、面试也延长了 15 分钟，你又补了一句 my apologies — I didn't find that issue in advance。
scenario_en: At the end of Round 3 the whiteboard permission problem had already been solved by the HM and the interview extended by 15 minutes, and you added "my apologies — I didn't find that issue in advance."
q: 这句额外的道歉该不该说？
q_en: Should you add that extra apology?
options: 该说，主动担责显得成熟，也让面试官知道你已经意识到了问题出在哪一环上
不该说，应该反过来说是工具方的问题，把责任推开，以保住这一轮最后的印象
该说，但要更长一些，把权限的日期、账号的问题都解释清楚，以示诚意和足够的透明度
不该重复道歉，换成一句行动：下次 onsite 前 24 小时我把工具全测一遍
options_en: Yes — taking responsibility looks mature and shows the interviewer you know where it went wrong.
No — say it was the tool vendor's problem instead, pushing the blame away to protect the round's impression.
Yes, and make it longer — explain the access dates and account issue in full to show sincerity and transparency.
Don't apologize twice; swap it for an action: before the next onsite I'll test every tool 24 hours ahead.
tradeoff: 行动收尾 vs 二次道歉：多道一次歉显得谦虚，代价是最后一句留给了自责而不是解决能力。
why: 道歉一次就够，第二次就变成填充词。把第二次道歉换成一句具体行动，收尾留下的是能解决问题的人。
why_en: One apology is enough and the second becomes filler, so replace it with a concrete action and let the last thing they hear be someone who fixes problems.
whenOtherWins: 如果失误确实由你造成、对方还没释怀，那就先完整道一次歉，再给补救方案。
optionMeanings: 把重复道歉当成担责的表现
把责任推给工具提供方
用更长的解释表达诚意
用一句具体行动替代二次道歉
optionMeanings_en: Treats a repeated apology as taking responsibility.
Shifts the blame onto the tool vendor.
Uses a longer explanation to show sincerity.
Replaces the second apology with a concrete action.
optionDirectness: 错在次数：第一次已经担过责了
错在方向：推责比多道一次歉更伤
错在长度：细节越多越像在自证
把收尾从情绪转成可执行的改进
optionDirectness_en: Wrong count — you already took responsibility the first time.
Wrong direction — deflecting hurts more than an extra apology.
Wrong length — the more detail, the more it sounds like self-justification.
Turns the closing line from emotion into an executable improvement.
optionScenarioImpacts: 最后一句留下的是自责，不是能力
对方刚帮你解决完，推责显得不领情
把一件已翻篇的事重新拉长
对方最后记住的是你会怎么防住下一次
optionScenarioImpacts_en: The last thing they hear is self-blame, not capability.
They just helped you fix it, so deflecting reads as ungrateful.
You stretch out something that was already closed.
What they remember is how you'll prevent it next time.

scenario: 你要讲 Meta 的项目，脑子里冒出一串名字：Business Suite、Click-to-Messenger、BSG AI、内部工单号。哪些能对外说，你需要一个判据。
scenario_en: You're about to describe a Meta project and a string of names comes to mind: Business Suite, Click-to-Messenger, BSG AI, an internal ticket ID. You need a rule for which ones can be said out loud.
q: 怎么判断一个词算不算内部黑话？
q_en: What test tells you whether a term counts as internal jargon?
options: 按保密级别判断：只要不是尚未公开的产品计划，其余的名字基本上都可以照说出来
按公司外有没有人用来判断：对外产品名可以说，内部简称和工单号要翻译
按对方背景判断：面试官是同行就照说，不是同行才换成通用词，临场看人下菜碟
统一按最保守的处理：所有名字都不提，一律说成「一个大型社交平台上的项目」
options_en: Judge by confidentiality: as long as it isn't an unannounced product plan, most names are fine to say.
Judge by whether anyone outside the company uses the term: public product names are fine, internal org shorthand and ticket IDs get translated or dropped.
Judge by who's listening: if the interviewer is from the same industry say it as-is, and only swap in generic terms otherwise.
Play it maximally safe: name nothing at all and just call it "a project on a large social platform."
tradeoff: 按外部通用度判断 vs 按保密级别判断：保密级别只管你能不能说，管不了对方听不听得懂。
why: 判据不是保密与否，是公司外有没有人用这个词。对外产品名（Business Suite）可以说，内部 org 简称和工单号必须翻译或省掉。
why_en: The test isn't confidentiality but whether anyone outside the company uses the word, so public product names stay and internal org shorthand gets translated or dropped.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方明确说过自己是前同事、并且先用了那个简称，跟着用反而是最快的对齐方式。

termDefinitions.meaning: Meta 内部对那个团队的简称；对外要说成「Business AI 团队」才有人听得懂。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BSG AI is Meta's internal shorthand for the Business Gen AI team; outsiders only follow it as "the Business AI team".

optionMeanings: 用保密级别当过滤器
用外部通用度当过滤器
按听众背景临场决定
一律不点名，全部模糊化
optionMeanings_en: Use confidentiality as the filter.
Use outside-the-company usage as the filter.
Decide on the fly based on the listener.
Name nothing and blur everything.
optionDirectness: 错在维度：能说和听得懂是两件事
同时管住了听得懂和边界感两条
错在可靠性：你猜不准对方懂哪些词
错在代价：模糊到对方无法评估你的经验
optionDirectness_en: Wrong dimension — being allowed to say it and being understood are different things.
Covers both comprehension and boundary awareness at once.
Unreliable — you can't guess which terms they actually know.
Costly — so vague they can't assess your experience at all.
optionScenarioImpacts: 合规过关了，对方还是一句没听懂
该说的说了，该翻的翻了，节奏不断
猜错一次就要停下来补解释
整段经历听起来像不能验证的空话
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You stay compliant and they still understand nothing.
The sayable gets said, the rest gets translated, and the rhythm holds.
One wrong guess and you stop to explain anyway.
The whole experience sounds unverifiable.

q: 内部黑话已经脱口而出了，当场怎么救？
q_en: The internal shorthand already slipped out — how do you recover mid-sentence?
text: 说漏之后用一个{{同位从句}}就地补翻译——「PRAC，也就是我们的 React 前端」——然后{{继续往下讲}}；不要停下来解释{{内部命名的来历}}。
text_en: Once it slips out, translate in place with an {{appositive clause}} — "PRAC, that's our React frontend" — then {{keep going}}; don't stop to explain {{where the internal name came from}}.
why: 补翻译只值一个从句。停下来讲内部命名的来历，会把一次口误拉成一段跑题，还显得你更像圈内人而不是候选人。
why_en: A slipped term is worth exactly one clause of repair — stopping to explain the internal naming history turns a small slip into a tangent and makes you sound like an insider rather than a candidate.

scenario: Elevate Health 那通电话，Otter 把你说的 full stack 转成了 food stack——full 词尾的 L 被吞掉了。
scenario_en: On the Elevate Health call, Otter transcribed your "full stack" as "food stack" — the L at the end of "full" got swallowed.
q: 这个发音问题该怎么定位和修？
q_en: How do you locate and fix that pronunciation problem?
options: 换个说法绕开这个词，改说 end-to-end engineer，避免每次都踩同一个坑
整体放慢语速，把每一个词都念重一点，用速度换清晰度，问题自然解决
词尾 L 要舌尖抵住上齿龈；普通话没有音节尾 L，最常见的失误是它脱落成元音
问题其实在元音上，把 full 里的 u 念成长音就能和 food 区分开来
options_en: Route around the word entirely and say "end-to-end engineer" so you never hit it.
Slow your whole delivery and hit every word harder, trading speed for clarity.
The final L needs the tongue tip on the ridge behind your teeth; Mandarin has no syllable-final L, so it usually collapses into a vowel.
The real issue is the vowel — lengthen the u in "full" and it separates from "food."
tradeoff: 定点修一个音 vs 整体放慢：放慢能提高可懂度，代价是每次自我介绍都被拖长，问题还在原地。
why: 普通话没有音节尾的 L，最常见的失误是把它元音化（table 听着像 tay-bow）。修法是练舌尖到位，不是放慢或绕开。
why_en: Mandarin has no syllable-final L, so it usually turns into a vowel — the fix is getting the tongue tip onto the ridge, not slowing down or avoiding the word.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方多次听不清的是整句而不是某个词，那才该先降语速、把句子切短。

termDefinitions.meaning: 英语音节末尾的 L，舌根抬起、舌尖仍要抵上齿龈；普通话没有这个位置的 L。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dark L is the English syllable-final L, where the back of the tongue raises but the tip still touches the ridge behind the teeth.

optionMeanings: 换词绕开，不碰这个音
用整体降速换清晰度
定位到词尾 L 的舌位问题
把问题归到元音长度上
optionMeanings_en: Swap the word and never make the sound.
Trade overall speed for clarity.
Locate it in the tongue position of the final L.
Attribute it to vowel length.
optionDirectness: 错在范围：这个音在别的词里还会再出现
错在层次：不清楚的是一个辅音，不是语速
对上了真正的成因，也给了可练的动作
错在归因：food 和 full 的差别在词尾辅音
optionDirectness_en: Too narrow — the same sound shows up in other words anyway.
Wrong level — a single consonant is unclear, not your speed.
Matches the real cause and gives you something to practise.
Wrong attribution — food and full differ in the final consonant.
optionScenarioImpacts: 自我介绍每次都要绕路，还是会被听错
整段自我介绍变慢，词还是含糊
练一个动作，所有词尾 L 一起改善
练错了地方，转写还是会出错
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Your intro detours every time and still gets misheard.
The whole intro slows down and the word stays mushy.
One drill fixes every final L at once.
You practise the wrong thing and the transcript still breaks.

scenario: 你想知道自己还有哪些词发音不清，但手边没有外教，也没人给你逐词反馈。
scenario_en: You want to know which words of yours are unclear, but you have no coach and nobody giving you word-level feedback.
q: 怎么低成本地自查发音问题？
q_en: What's a low-cost way to audit your own pronunciation?
options: 对着发音词典逐词跟读，把自我介绍里的所有生词和长词都覆盖一遍
用转写工具录一遍自我介绍，看它把哪些词转错——转错的就是发音信号
让朋友听一遍并指出问题，人耳比机器准，给的反馈也更具体更可操作
把语速降到平时的一半录一遍，如果慢速下听得清就说明发音其实没问题
options_en: Shadow a pronunciation dictionary word by word, covering every long or unfamiliar word in your intro.
Record your intro through a transcription tool and see which words come out wrong — those are your pronunciation flags.
Have a friend listen and point out problems; human ears are more accurate and the feedback is more specific.
Record at half your normal speed — if it's clear when slow, your pronunciation is fine.
tradeoff: 机器转写 vs 找人听：人耳能给更具体的口型建议，代价是不能天天做，也记不住哪些词反复出错。
why: 转写工具对模糊音最敏感——food stack 就是这么暴露的。它免费、可重复，而且只标出真正听不清的词。
why_en: Transcription tools are the most sensitive detector of mushy sounds — that's how "food stack" surfaced — and they're free, repeatable, and flag only the words that truly aren't clear.
whenOtherWins: 如果转写全对但对方仍反复要你重复，那问题在语调和断句，需要真人反馈。
optionMeanings: 逐词跟读词典标准音
用转写错误定位问题词
靠人耳给主观反馈
用慢速录音判断清晰度
optionMeanings_en: Shadow dictionary pronunciations word by word.
Use transcription errors to locate problem words.
Rely on a human ear for subjective feedback.
Judge clarity from a slowed-down recording.
optionDirectness: 错在效率：不知道该练哪些词，覆盖成本高
把「哪些词不清楚」变成可重复的清单
只有需要口型和舌位建议时才更划算
错在条件：面试里没有半速这个选项
optionDirectness_en: Inefficient — you don't know which words to drill, so coverage costs a lot.
Turns "which words are unclear" into a repeatable list.
Only worth it when you need mouth-shape and tongue-position advice.
Wrong condition — half speed isn't available in a real interview.
optionScenarioImpacts: 练了很多词，真正出错的那个可能没练到
拿到一份具体词表，可以逐个攻
反馈好但频次低，问题词记不全
结论虚假：正常语速下照样被听错
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You drill many words and may miss the one that actually breaks.
You get a concrete word list you can work through.
Good feedback but too infrequent to track every problem word.
A false all-clear — at normal speed it still gets misheard.

scenario: 教练指出你的英语像念稿：语调平、直接进细节。而面试官需要边听边在纸上记要点。
scenario_en: The coach flagged that your English sounds like reading a script — flat intonation, straight into details — while the interviewer is trying to take notes as you speak.
q: 一段口头回答该怎么组织，方便对方记笔记？
q_en: How should a spoken answer be organized so the other side can take notes?
options: 按时间顺序讲：先讲背景是怎么来的，再讲中间过程，最后才给结论和影响
第一句先总述这段要讲什么，再一二三分点展开，用语调把各点分层
把最有冲击力的数字放在开头，其余细节按自己想到的顺序补充上去
每讲完一点就停下来问对方还想不想继续听，用互动来代替固定结构
options_en: Go chronologically: how the situation arose, then the middle, then the conclusion and impact last.
Open with one topic sentence saying what this answer covers, then break it into first, second, third, using intonation to separate the points.
Put the most striking number first and add the remaining details in whatever order they come to you.
Pause after each point to ask whether they want to hear more, replacing structure with interaction.
tradeoff: 总述加分点 vs 时间顺序：按时间讲更自然，代价是听的人到最后才知道重点在哪，笔记记不下来。
why: 面试官要在纸上留下要点。第一句总述给他一个标题，一二三给他三条可记的行，语调分层告诉他新的一条开始了。
why_en: The interviewer needs points on paper, so the opening sentence gives them a heading, the numbered points give them rows to write, and shifting intonation tells them a new row started.
whenOtherWins: 讲一个故事型 BQ 时，时间顺序本身就是结构——但仍要用一句话先说清结论。
optionMeanings: 用时间线组织整段
先总述再分点，语调分层
用最强的数字开场
用互动代替结构
optionMeanings_en: Organize the whole answer along a timeline.
Topic sentence first, then numbered points with layered intonation.
Open with the strongest number.
Replace structure with interaction.
optionDirectness: 错在时机：结论压到最后，笔记没有标题
同时解决了标题、条目和分隔三件事
错在结构：有钩子但后面无法归类
错在负担：把组织的责任推给了面试官
optionDirectness_en: Wrong timing — the conclusion arrives last and the notes have no heading.
Solves the heading, the rows, and the separators all at once.
Structurally weak — a hook with nothing to file the rest under.
Shifts the burden of organizing onto the interviewer.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方听完才知道重点，回头补不了笔记
笔记上留下清晰的三行，debrief 才有据可引
开头亮眼，后面越听越散
打断多，整段被切碎，时间也超
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They only learn the point at the end and can't backfill their notes.
Three clean lines land on paper and can be quoted at the debrief.
A bright opening that scatters as it goes.
Constant interruptions fragment the answer and overrun the time.

scenario: 面试官问了一个开放技术问题，你有约两分钟。目标是让他在纸上留下可引用的要点。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks an open technical question and you have about two minutes; the goal is to leave quotable points on their notepad.
q: 把「让面试官能记笔记」的一段回答排成正确顺序。
q_en: Put the four beats of a note-friendly spoken answer in order.
steps: 分点展开，每点开头把语调抬高，提示这是新的一条
第一句总述：这段要回答的是什么、结论是什么
收一句可带走的规则或代价，把话头交回去
点明这段有几点：我从三个方面说
why: 总述给标题、报数量给格子、语调分层给分隔线、收尾给一句可引用的话。四步缺一步，笔记就会糊成一团。
why_en: The topic sentence gives a heading, announcing the count gives them rows, intonation gives the dividers, and the closing line gives them something to quote.

scenario: 教练点名你的一句表达是中文直译：the faster the feature is implemented, the more they stack up in the release stage。
scenario_en: The coach flagged one of your sentences as a literal translation from Chinese: "the faster the feature is implemented, the more they stack up in the release stage."
q: 这句话该怎么改，才能让面试官一听就懂？
q_en: How should that sentence be rewritten so the interviewer gets it first time?
options: 结构不动，只把用词换准一点，语法本身没错，对方能自己推出意思来
拆成两个短句，先说事实再说后果：发布不可靠，功能做得越快，卡在发布阶段的越多
加一句 what I mean is 再解释一遍，用重复来补上第一遍表达得不清楚的地方
换成更书面的从句结构，用更正式的连接词，让整句听起来更专业更有分量
options_en: Keep the structure and just pick better words — the grammar is fine and they can work out the meaning.
Split it into two short sentences, fact first then consequence: releases weren't reliable, so the faster features got built, the more piled up waiting to ship.
Add "what I mean is" and explain it again, using repetition to patch what the first attempt didn't convey.
Rewrite it with a more formal subordinate clause and heavier connectors so it sounds more professional.
tradeoff: 拆短句 vs 补一句解释：补解释能救回意思，代价是同一件事说了两遍，时间和节奏一起丢。
why: 中式直译的问题不是语法，是把两层意思压进一个长句。拆成短句、先事实后后果，对方不用回放就懂。
why_en: The problem with a literal translation isn't grammar but cramming two ideas into one long clause, so split it — fact first, consequence second — and they get it without rewinding.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方明确说没听懂某个词，那就直接换那个词并给一个例子，不必重构整句。
optionMeanings: 保留长句结构，只换词
拆成事实句加后果句
重复解释一遍来补救
改成更正式的从句
optionMeanings_en: Keep the long clause and swap words only.
Split into a fact sentence plus a consequence sentence.
Patch it by explaining a second time.
Rewrite it as a more formal subordinate clause.
optionDirectness: 错在根因：难懂的是句子结构，不是选词
抓住了「一句只装一个意思」这条口语规则
错在成本：同一件事说两遍，节奏被吃掉
错在方向：更长的从句只会更难听懂
optionDirectness_en: Misses the cause — the structure is what's hard, not the word choice.
Applies the spoken-language rule of one idea per sentence.
Costly — saying the same thing twice eats your rhythm.
Wrong direction — a longer clause is harder to follow, not easier.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方还是要在脑子里回放一遍
两句都能被直接记下来
面试官记下「表达需要反复澄清」
越正式越像书面语，口头更难跟
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They still have to replay it in their head.
Both sentences can be written down as-is.
The interviewer notes that your points need repeated clarification.
The more formal it gets, the harder it is to follow live.

scenario: Round 3/4 你有几次盯着字幕、在脑子里译成中文再理解，反应慢了半拍还答偏了题，面试官表情明显变差。
scenario_en: In Rounds 3 and 4 you sometimes stared at the captions and translated into Chinese in your head, answering half a beat late and off-target, and the interviewer's expression visibly changed.
q: 怎么把「先翻译再理解」这一层去掉？
q_en: How do you remove that translate-then-understand layer?
options: 关掉字幕只靠听，逼自己适应，时间长了自然就不再依赖翻译这一层
让面试官把每一个问题都重复一遍，用重复来换取自己的理解时间
会前用英文出声热身，答题时抓住问题里的那个约束词直接用英文往下想
把常见问题的中文答案背熟，现场再一句一句译成英文说出来，稳妥又不会漏点
options_en: Turn the captions off and rely on listening, forcing yourself to adapt until the translation habit fades.
Ask the interviewer to repeat every question, trading repetition for comprehension time.
Warm up out loud in English before the call, then latch onto the constraint word in the question and reason forward in English.
Memorize Chinese answers to common questions and translate them sentence by sentence on the spot.
tradeoff: 英文直想 vs 中译英：先在中文里想更有把握，代价是慢半拍，还容易把约束译丢、答偏题。
why: 中间那层翻译既慢又会丢约束。会前把语言切到英文，答题时只锁住问题里的那个约束词，绕开逐句翻译。
why_en: That middle translation layer is both slow and lossy, so switch into English before the call and lock onto the one constraint word in the question instead of translating sentence by sentence.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方口音重或术语生僻，那就针对那一个词请他确认，而不是让整个问题重来。
optionMeanings: 靠断掉字幕强行适应
靠对方重复换理解时间
会前切语言，答题锁约束词
背中文答案现场逐句翻译
optionMeanings_en: Force adaptation by cutting the captions.
Buy comprehension time by asking for repeats.
Switch language before the call and lock onto the constraint word.
Memorize Chinese answers and translate live.
optionDirectness: 错在工具：字幕不是原因，翻译习惯才是
错在次数：反复要求重复会被读成没在听
把语言切换提前，现场只剩理解和组织
错在路径：这是把翻译层固化下来
optionDirectness_en: Blames the tool — captions aren't the cause, the translating habit is.
Wrong frequency — repeated requests read as not listening.
Moves the language switch earlier so only comprehension is left live.
Wrong path — this hard-codes the translation layer in.

scenario: Amazon Round 1 是 BQ 加 OOD 编码共约 57 分钟。BQ 追问拖到约 25 分钟，编码只剩 25 分钟，最后一个折扣策略没写完。
scenario_en: Amazon Round 1 was behavioral plus OOD coding in about 57 minutes. The behavioral follow-ups ran to roughly 25 minutes, leaving only 25 for coding, and the last discount strategy never got finished.
q: 开场就该做的时间管理动作是什么？
q_en: What time-management move belongs at the very start of the round?
options: 先把 BQ 讲透，编码部分靠临场加速，代码本身熟练就能把时间补回来
开场在纸上写下各环节的分钟预算，全程看表，超了就当场压缩
编码开始时再看一眼时间，按剩下多少分钟决定代码要写到多细
把最难的折扣策略放到最后写，就算写不完也不影响整体的类结构
options_en: Cover the behavioral part fully and make up the time by coding faster, since you know the patterns.
Write a per-section minute budget on paper at the start, watch the clock throughout, and compress on the spot when you overrun.
Check the clock once coding begins and let the remaining minutes decide how detailed the code gets.
Save the hardest discount strategy for last, so an unfinished one doesn't damage the overall class structure.
tradeoff: 先定预算 vs 讲到哪算哪：不设预算能把每题讲透，代价是最后一段被时间腰斩。
why: 时间预算要在开口前写下来并全程看表。BQ 每题主答约 2 分钟、追问 2–3 句收口，编码才留得下 30 分钟。
why_en: Write the minute budget down before you start talking and keep watching the clock — two minutes per behavioral answer and two or three sentences per follow-up is what leaves thirty minutes to code.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明说这轮只考 BQ、编码只是走个形式，那就把时间全押在追问的深度上。
optionMeanings: 把补时间的希望压在编码速度上
开场写下预算并全程看表
到编码时再按剩余时间决定深度
靠调整写作顺序降低损失
optionMeanings_en: Bet on coding speed to recover the time.
Write the budget at the start and watch the clock.
Decide depth by whatever minutes remain when coding starts.
Reorder what you write to limit the damage.
optionDirectness: 错在假设：追问的长度不由你单方面决定
把时间变成可见变量，超时能当场发现
错在时机：发现时窗口已经关上了
错在层次：调顺序治不了总时长不够
optionDirectness_en: Bad assumption — you don't control how long the follow-ups run.
Makes time a visible variable you can catch overrunning live.
Wrong timing — by then the window has already closed.
Wrong level — reordering doesn't fix a total-time shortfall.
optionScenarioImpacts: 编码开始时已经晚了，加速也补不回来
追问一超时就能当场收口，编码时间保住
只能被动砍深度，结构讲不完整
最后一个策略还是写不完，问题没变
optionScenarioImpacts_en: By the time coding starts you're already behind and speed can't recover it.
You can close a follow-up the moment it overruns and protect the coding time.
You can only cut depth reactively and the structure stays incomplete.
The last strategy still doesn't get finished — nothing changed.

scenario: 系统设计讲到一半你抬头看表，只剩 8 分钟，而计划里还有三个深挖点没讲。
scenario_en: Halfway through a system design you check the clock: eight minutes left and three deep-dive points still unspoken.
q: 剩余时间不够时怎么处理？
q_en: What do you do when the remaining time doesn't fit the plan?
options: 加快语速把三个点都念完，信息量优先，覆盖面比讲得慢更重要
跳过剩下的点，直接问面试官他还有什么想问的，把主动权交出去
把最复杂的那个点讲透，另外两个留到最后的反问环节再补回来
挑一个最能体现判断的点展开，其余各一句带过，留一句收尾
options_en: Speed up and get all three out, prioritizing coverage over pace.
Skip the rest and ask the interviewer what else they'd like to cover, handing over control.
Do the most complex one properly and save the other two for the questions-for-us section at the end.
Expand the one that best shows judgement, give the others a sentence each, and keep one line to close.
tradeoff: 取一展开、其余一句带过 vs 全部加速讲完：全讲能覆盖更多，代价是没有一个点留下判断的痕迹。
why: 时间不够就讲简单点，最理想是正好说完。加速念完等于把三个点都讲成了听不清的半句。
why_en: When time is short, say less rather than faster — racing through three points just turns all three into half-sentences nobody can follow.
whenOtherWins: 如果剩下的点里有一个是面试官刚点名想听的，那就先讲那一个，别按自己的顺序走。
optionMeanings: 用语速换覆盖面
提前收口，把选择权交回去
只讲最难的一个，其余延后
一个展开，其余各一句带过
optionMeanings_en: Trade pace for coverage.
Close early and hand the choice back.
Cover only the hardest one and defer the rest.
Expand one and give the others a sentence each.
optionDirectness: 错在可懂度：说得快等于三个点都没讲清
只有当对方已经在收尾时才合适
错在场次：反问环节不是补设计的地方
把有限时间投在最能显判断的那一处
optionDirectness_en: Fails on comprehension — speeding up means none of the three lands.
Only fits when they're already wrapping up.
Wrong slot — the Q&A section isn't where you finish a design.
Puts the scarce minutes where judgement shows most.
optionScenarioImpacts: 笔记上一条都留不下，等于没讲
对方会觉得你自己也不知道还剩什么
反问环节被占，实质问题问不出来
至少有一个点被完整记住，还留了收尾
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Nothing lands on their notepad, so it may as well not have been said.
They sense you don't know what's left either.
The Q&A slot gets eaten and your real questions never get asked.
At least one point is remembered in full and you still close cleanly.

scenario: OOD 题要三种折扣策略：percentage、BUY_X_GET_Y、FIXED_OFF。你对 BUY_X_GET_Y 的语义最熟，percentage 反而讲不出新意。
scenario_en: The OOD question needs three discount strategies: percentage, BUY_X_GET_Y, and FIXED_OFF. You know the BUY_X_GET_Y semantics best and have nothing fresh to say about percentage.
q: 时间有限时，深度该往哪儿放？
q_en: With limited time, where should the depth go?
options: 多讲 BUY_X_GET_Y 的语义和边界，percentage 一句带过
先讲最不熟的 percentage，把风险最高的地方趁早过掉，剩下的都好说
平均分配时间，三种策略讲一样多，保证覆盖完整、没有明显的短板
三种都只给接口签名，把省下的时间全留给整体类图和扩展性讨论
options_en: Spend the time on BUY_X_GET_Y semantics and edge cases, and give percentage one sentence.
Start with percentage since you know it least, clearing the riskiest part early so the rest is easy.
Split time evenly across all three so coverage is complete and there's no obvious weak spot.
Give only interface signatures for all three and spend the saved time on the class diagram and extensibility.
tradeoff: 集中深挖擅长项 vs 平均覆盖：平均分配看着完整，代价是没有任何一处显出判断力。
why: 把话题往自己最熟的方向引，是时间管理的一部分。深度只在一个点上出现，比三个点都浅有效得多。
why_en: Steering toward what I know best is part of managing the clock, because depth in one place reads far stronger than three shallow passes.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官点名要看某一种策略，那必须先满足他的指定，再把深度放到擅长的那块。
optionMeanings: 把深度压在最熟的那一种
先攻最不熟的一种
三种平均分配时间
都只给签名，转向类图
optionMeanings_en: Concentrate depth on the one you know best.
Tackle the least familiar one first.
Split time evenly across the three.
Give signatures only and pivot to the class diagram.
optionDirectness: 把有限时间换成一处可被追问的深度
错在风险：最不熟的地方最容易被问穿
错在效果：三处都浅，没有可追问的落点
错在取舍：类图不缺，缺的是语义细节
optionDirectness_en: Converts limited time into one area deep enough to be probed.
Risky — the least familiar area is where a follow-up breaks you.
Ineffective — three shallow passes leave nothing to probe.
Wrong tradeoff — the diagram isn't what's missing; the semantics are.
optionScenarioImpacts: 追问落在你最强的地方，越问越好
开局就暴露弱项，后面节奏全乱
面试官记不下任何一个有判断的点
结构清楚但没有一处显出真实经验
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Follow-ups land where you're strongest and it gets better as they dig.
You expose the weak spot early and the rhythm never recovers.
The interviewer can't write down a single point of judgement.
The structure is clear but nothing shows real experience.

q: BQ 环节的时间预算该怎么切，编码才留得下时间？
q_en: How do you budget the behavioral section so coding still has room?
text: 每个 BQ 主答控制在约 {{2 分钟}}，每个追问用 {{2–3 句}}收口；这样 57 分钟的 BQ 加编码轮才能给编码留下 {{30}} 分钟以上。
text_en: Keep each behavioral answer to about {{two minutes}} and close each follow-up in {{two or three sentences}}; that's what leaves more than {{30}} minutes for coding in a 57-minute combined round.
why: 追问是时间被拉长的主要来源。主答 2 分钟、追问 2–3 句，是把编码时间守住的唯一办法。
why_en: Follow-ups are where the time goes, so two minutes per main answer and two or three sentences per follow-up is the only way to protect the coding block.

scenario: 教练定调：能用 AI 就用，但不是随便生成一个就交上去。对 coding 面试的含义是——手写的门槛已经很低了。
scenario_en: The coach's line: use AI whenever you can, but not by shipping whatever it generates. For coding interviews that means the bar for writing by hand is now low.
q: 在允许用 AI 的编码轮里，标准是什么？
q_en: In a coding round where AI is allowed, what's the bar?
options: 自己从头手写，完全不碰 AI，既避免被怀疑，也能证明自己的基本功还在
让 AI 生成之后直接提交，只要能跑就行，把省下的时间留给后面的讨论环节
生成前就知道它大概会输出什么，看到之后立刻能说清每一行为什么这么写
先自己写一版，再让 AI 优化一版，两版都保留下来给面试官对比着看
options_en: Write everything by hand and don't touch AI, avoiding suspicion and proving your fundamentals.
Submit whatever the model generates as long as it runs, saving the time for the discussion afterwards.
Know roughly what it will produce before you ask, and be able to explain every line the moment you see it.
Write your own version first, have AI optimize a second one, and show the interviewer both to compare.
tradeoff: 先有预期再用 vs 直接提交生成结果：直接提交最快，代价是被追问任意一行就露馅。
why: 门槛从「能不能手写」变成「看到之后能不能立刻反应过来」。说不清为什么这么写，就是失去了掌控。
why_en: The bar moved from writing it yourself to recognizing it instantly — if you can't say why a line is there, you've lost control of the code.
whenOtherWins: 如果这一轮明确禁止任何辅助工具，那就完全手写，并且先把思路说出声再敲键盘。
optionMeanings: 彻底不用，靠手写证明能力
生成即提交，只看能不能跑
带着预期用，逐行能解释
两版并存，交给面试官比较
optionMeanings_en: Refuse AI entirely and prove ability by hand.
Generate and submit, judged only by whether it runs.
Use it with an expectation and explain it line by line.
Keep both versions and let the interviewer compare.
optionDirectness: 只有明确禁用工具的轮次才需要这么做
错在验收：能跑不等于你说得清它在干嘛
把可解释性设成验收标准，而不是来源
错在成本：写两版把时间花在了展示上
optionDirectness_en: Only needed in rounds that explicitly ban tools.
Wrong acceptance test — running isn't the same as being able to explain it.
Makes explainability the acceptance criterion rather than the code's origin.
Costly — writing twice spends the time on presentation.

第一个追问就问到你答不上来的那一行
工具帮你提速，判断仍然是你的
时间被切成两半，两版都讲不深
optionScenarioImpacts_en: You waste the efficiency you were allowed and run tighter on time.
The first follow-up lands on the line you can't explain.
The tool speeds you up while the judgement stays yours.
Time splits in two and neither version gets explained deeply.

scenario: 你自己踩过的坑：AI 写的一段代码上线就触发告警，而且 bug 极难复现，因为当时没人说得清它为什么那么写。
scenario_en: Your own experience: a block of AI-written code alerted the moment it shipped, and the bug was nearly impossible to reproduce because nobody could say why it was written that way.
q: 这段经历说明「失去掌控」的代价出现在哪个环节？
q_en: In that experience, at which stage does losing control actually cost you?
options: 出现在写代码时：AI 生成得太快，人跟不上它的节奏，来不及逐行确认
出现在 review 时：reviewer 看不懂它的写法和风格，合不进主干分支
出现在故障时：没人能解释它的行为，复现和定位都失去了起点
出现在交付时：AI 代码的风格不统一，后续维护和改动的成本变高
why: 代价不在写的时候，在出事的时候。解释不了的代码，一旦线上告警就没有排查的起点。
why_en: The cost doesn't land while you write it but when it breaks — code nobody can explain leaves you with no starting point once the alert fires.

把代价定位在代码评审上
把代价定位在线上排障上
把代价定位在长期维护上

Locates the cost in code review.
Locates the cost in production debugging.
Locates the cost in long-term maintenance.
optionDirectness: 速度可以放慢，这不是不可逆的那一项
评审能拦下风格问题，拦不下语义盲区
对上了「难复现」这个最贵的后果
维护成本真实，但不会让你当晚被叫醒
optionDirectness_en: Speed can be slowed down; it isn't the irreversible part.
Review can catch style but not a semantic blind spot.
Matches the most expensive symptom: it couldn't be reproduced.
Maintenance cost is real but it won't page you at night.
optionScenarioImpacts: 会让你只是放慢生成，盲区还在
会让你依赖评审兜底，兜不住
解释了为什么必须逐行能说清
会让你去统一风格，修错了地方
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Leads you to just generate slower while the blind spot remains.
Leads you to lean on review, which can't catch it.
Explains why every line has to be explainable.
Sends you to unify style — the wrong fix.
options_en: It lands while writing: the model generates faster than you can follow, leaving no time to check line by line.
It lands in review: reviewers cannot follow its style, so it never merges into the main branch.
It lands in an incident: nobody can explain its behaviour, so reproducing and locating the bug has no starting point.
It lands at handover: inconsistent style raises the cost of every later change and fix.

scenario: Amazon Round 3 当天你打不开 Bluescape——账号权限只开到 7/6–7/7，HM 只能临时换白板，白丢约 15 分钟，系统设计从第 58 分钟才真正开始。
scenario_en: On the day of Amazon Round 3 you couldn't open Bluescape — your access had only been provisioned for 7/6–7/7 — so the HM had to switch whiteboards, burning about 15 minutes and pushing the system design to minute 58.
q: 这类工具故障该在什么时候、怎么排掉？
q_en: When and how should that kind of tool failure be cleared?
options: 提前 24 小时用真实账号打开白板并画一笔，确认权限当天有效
面试当天提前 10 分钟登录一次，真出问题还来得及去找 recruiter 协调

准备好 Excalidraw 之类的备用白板，当天真出问题就现场切换过去继续画
options_en: Open the whiteboard with your real account 24 hours ahead and actually draw something to confirm access holds.

why: 权限是有有效期的，能收到链接不等于当天能进。提前 24 小时用真实账号真的画一笔，才算测过。

whenOtherWins: 如果工具是面试当场才开房间发链接的，那就把备用白板和屏幕共享提前练熟。

Prepare a fallback tool for failures.

发现时已无解，只能占用面试时间

scenario: onsite 前 24 小时，你要用面试当天会用的那个真实账号，把当天要用到的东西全部真操作一遍。
scenario_en: Twenty-four hours before the onsite you run through everything you'll use on the day, with the same real account you'll use then.
q: 这份 24 小时 checklist 该包含哪些项？
q_en: What belongs on that 24-hour checklist?
options: 打开邀请里指定的白板工具，真的画一笔并保存，确认权限当天仍然有效

scenario: 面试官问你用没用过 Temporal。你没用过，但做过带重试和状态恢复的长任务流程。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks whether you've used Temporal. You haven't, but you have built long-running task flows with retries and state recovery.
q: 没用过的工具该怎么答，才不踩禁语？
q_en: How do you answer about a tool you've never used without hitting the banned phrase?
options: 直说没用过、也不太熟，然后就停在这里，等他换下一个问题继续往下问别的东西
含糊说自己接触过一点点，避免直说没用过，赌他不会继续往细节里追问下去，蒙过这一题
反问他们团队具体拿它做什么，把问题交回去，等他解释完自己再决定怎么表态回应
说没直接用过，但做过带重试和状态恢复的任务流，我理解它的核心是持久化的工作流编排
options_en: Say plainly you haven't used it and aren't familiar, then stop and wait for the next question.
Vaguely claim some exposure to avoid saying no outright, betting they won't dig into details.
Ask what their team uses it for, handing the question back and waiting to react to their answer.
Say you haven't used it directly but have built retrying, state-recovering task flows, and that you understand its core to be durable workflow orchestration.
tradeoff: bridge 模板 vs 直接说不熟：直说更省事，代价是话头断在这里，你的类似经验一句都没进对方笔记。
why: 「没用过」不是禁语，「我不熟」才是。用「没直接用过 + 类似经验 + 我理解它的核心是什么」把话接下去。
why_en: Saying I haven't used it is fine; saying I'm not familiar with it is not — so bridge with what I have built and what I understand its core idea to be.
whenOtherWins: 如果对方要的是这门技术的实操年限（岗位硬性要求），那就直接给事实，别用类比绕。

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个持久化工作流编排引擎：长任务的状态会被持久保存，进程崩溃重启后能从断点继续。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Temporal is a durable workflow orchestration engine that persists long-running task state so a crashed process can resume where it left off.

scenario: GenLogs 那轮你先说「我在 Meta 和 TikTok 都做过云基础设施」，紧接着又说「AWS 我没用过，但我会学」。
scenario_en: On the GenLogs call you said "I worked on cloud infrastructure at both Meta and TikTok," then immediately added "I haven't used AWS, but I'll learn it."
q: 这两句连在一起的问题出在哪？
q_en: What goes wrong when those two sentences land back to back?
options: 两句自相矛盾，先立起来的可信度被后一句抵消，对方两句都不信
问题在第二句太谦虚，应该改成说自己已经在系统地自学 AWS 了
问题在第一句说得太满，应该先坦白自己没有公有云的实战经验
问题只在顺序上，把「我会学」放前面、把经验放后面就不会有矛盾了
options_en: They contradict each other — the second sentence cancels the credibility the first one built, so they believe neither.
The second sentence is too modest; it should say you're already studying AWS systematically.
The first sentence overclaims; you should lead by admitting you have no public-cloud experience.
It's purely an ordering issue — put "I'll learn it" first and the experience second and the contradiction disappears.
tradeoff: 一段连贯的桥 vs 先立后拆：分两句说更诚实，代价是听的人只记住了矛盾本身。
why: 一句话立起来的可信度，被下一句自己拆掉。正确讲法是一段话：内部自研云 → 概念相同 → AWS 的具体差异我在补。
why_en: The credibility built by the first sentence gets dismantled by the second, so say it as one arc: in-house cloud, same core concepts, and I'm filling in the AWS specifics.
whenOtherWins: 如果岗位硬性要求 AWS 认证或实操年限，就直接给事实，不要用内部云去桥。
